auto.reason: GLO-30 (1 arc-second) where the box is small: at most 80 M working cells (for example 3 x 2 degrees). The GPU passes allocate at most 28 bytes per cell (flat-resolution stage, counted from the allocations in src/gpu.rs), about 2.2 GB at the limit; the whole build peaked at 896 MB host memory for the 25.9 M-cell GLO-30 CONUS check box on an RTX 5070 Ti (35 bytes per cell), about 2.8 GB at the limit.

GLO-90 (3 arc-seconds) for every larger box up to 250 M working cells; the Rhine box 4-12E 46-52N is 69.1 M cells and builds in 2.4 s on an RTX 5070 Ti (24 threads, 1.85 GB peak host memory). Above 250 M cells (continental and global boxes) the working grid is the GLO-90 grid coarsened by the smallest integer factor that fits, each cell the block mean of the GLO-90 cells it holds, so any box on Earth builds: at 3 arc-seconds the 86 x 46 degree 12 km continental domain is 5.7 G cells (about 160 GB GPU, 200 GB host at the 28 and 35 bytes per cell above); coarsened by 5 to 15 arc-seconds it is 228 M cells and built in 2 min 20 s on a shared 24-thread node (8.6 GB peak host memory, 740,474 flowpaths, 0 contract errors).
